Turkish · 1,000 words

Turkish words 301–400

Turkish words 301 to 400, by how often they're used, each with its meaning in English, an example sentence and, for verbs, the main forms (he, she or it). 84 of them are taught in the lessons of the course.

Learn them with spaced repetition, Anki-style: open the flashcards. Free, no account needed.

  1. 301
    korumakverb

    to protect; to keep, to preserve

    Seni her zaman korurum.

    I'll always protect you.

    aorist korur · present koruyor · past korudu · future koruyacak

    What you protect from takes the ablative: güneşten korumak (to protect from the sun).

    A2· Conjugation

  2. 302
    güçnoun

    strength, power; force; difficult (adj)

    Hiç gücüm kalmadı.

    I have no strength left.

    accusative gücü

    ç becomes c before a vowel: gücü. As an adjective (formal), difficult: güç bir karar. Güçlü = strong.

    B2First taught in B2 · Unit 1: Unreal conditionals and wishes

  3. 303
    kesinlikleadverb

    definitely, absolutely; certainly

    Kesinlikle haklısın.

    You're absolutely right.

    From kesin (certain). Kesinlikle hayır! = Absolutely not!

    C1First taught in C1 · Unit 2: -DIr: assumption and authority

  4. 304
    sıranoun

    turn; row, line; order; desk (at school)

    Sıra sende.

    It's your turn.

    Sıra beklemek = to wait in line; sırayla = in turn, one by one.

    A2First taught in A2 · Unit 11: While and then

  5. 305
    akşamnoun

    evening; in the evening

    Akşam yemeği saat yedide.

    Dinner is at seven.

    Akşamları = in the evenings; İyi akşamlar = Good evening.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 7: To and from

  6. 306
    okumakverb

    to read; to study (at school)

    Yatakta kitap okuyorum.

    I'm reading a book in bed.

    aorist okur · present okuyor · past okudu · future okuyacak

    Also to study at a school: Tıp okuyor (She's studying medicine).

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 6: The present continuous· Conjugation

  7. 307
    okulnoun

    school

    Okul saat sekizde başlıyor.

    School starts at eight.

    Okula gitmek = to go to school; okul arkadaşı = school friend.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 2: Vowel harmony and plurals

  8. 308
    savaşnoun

    war; fight, battle

    Savaş çok uzun sürdü.

    The war went on for a very long time.

    Savaşmak = to fight; savaş filmi = war movie.

    B2First taught in B2 · Unit 3: Although, despite, without

  9. 309
    yarınadverb

    tomorrow

    Yarın hava güzel olacak.

    The weather will be nice tomorrow.

    Yarın sabah = tomorrow morning; öbür gün = the day after tomorrow.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 6: The present continuous

  10. 310
    yetmekverb

    to be enough

    Bu kadar yeter!

    That's enough!

    aorist yeter · present yetiyor · past yetti · future yetecek

    Yeter! = Enough! Stop it! The person takes the dative: Bu para bana yeter (This money is enough for me).

    A2· Conjugation

  11. 311
    ummakverb

    to hope; to expect

    Umarım yakında görüşürüz.

    I hope we'll see each other soon.

    aorist umar · present umuyor · past umdu · future umacak

    Mostly as Umarım (I hope) at the start of a sentence.

    B2First taught in B2 · Unit 1: Unreal conditionals and wishes· Conjugation

  12. 312
    dikkatnoun

    attention; care; Careful! Watch out! (Dikkat!)

    Dikkat, yer ıslak!

    Careful, the floor is wet!

    accusative dikkati

    Takes front-vowel suffixes: dikkati. Dikkat etmek = to be careful, to pay attention, with the dative: Yola dikkat et!

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 12: Requests and company

  13. 313
    oyunnoun

    game; play (theatre); trick

    Çocuklar bahçede oyun oynuyor.

    The kids are playing a game in the garden.

    Oyun oynamak = to play a game; bilgisayar oyunu = video game. Also a stage play.

    A2First taught in A2 · Unit 2: Was, were, and once upon a time

  14. 314
    açıkadjective

    open; light (of colours); clear

    Market pazar günü açık mı?

    Is the supermarket open on Sunday?

    Of colours, light: açık mavi. The opposite is kapalı (closed) or koyu (dark).

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 4: Questions and negation

  15. 315
    kabul etmekverb

    to accept; to agree to; to admit

    Özrünü kabul ediyorum.

    I accept your apology.

    aorist kabul eder · present kabul ediyor · past kabul etti · future kabul edecek

    What you accept takes the accusative: teklifi kabul etmek. Kabul! = Agreed!

    B2First taught in B2 · Unit 1: Unreal conditionals and wishes· Conjugation

  16. 316
    yürümekverb

    to walk

    Her sabah parkta yürürüm.

    I walk in the park every morning.

    aorist yürür · present yürüyor · past yürüdü · future yürüyecek

    Yürüyerek = on foot; yürüyüşe çıkmak = to go for a walk.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 7: To and from· Conjugation

  17. 317
    affetmekverb

    to forgive; to excuse

    Lütfen beni affet.

    Please forgive me.

    aorist affeder · present affediyor · past affetti · future affedecek

    Affedersiniz = Excuse me. t becomes d before a vowel: affediyor.

    B2First taught in B2 · Unit 9: Everyday colloquial Turkish· Conjugation

  18. 318
    niyeadverb

    why

    Niye gülüyorsun?

    Why are you laughing?

    More casual than neden and niçin.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 4: Questions and negation

  19. 319
    yanlışadjective

    wrong, incorrect; mistake (noun)

    Galiba yanlış otobüse bindik.

    I think we got on the wrong bus.

    As a noun, mistake. Yanlış anlama = Don't get me wrong. The opposite is doğru.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 4: Questions and negation

  20. 320
    bulunmakverb

    to be (somewhere), to be located; to be found

    Otel şehir merkezinde bulunuyor.

    The hotel is in the city centre.

    aorist bulunur · present bulunuyor · past bulundu · future bulunacak

    A more formal to be for places. Also the passive of bulmak: Cüzdanım bulundu (My wallet was found).

    B1First taught in B1 · Unit 10: Passive and reflexive· Conjugation

  21. 321
    amaninterjection

    oh no, oh dear; for goodness' sake

    Aman, çok geç kaldım!

    Oh no, I'm really late!

    Shows worry, surprise or annoyance. Aman dikkat! = Be careful!

    A2

  22. 322
    kocanoun

    husband; huge, big (adj)

    Kocam öğretmen.

    My husband is a teacher.

    Eş is the neutral word for spouse. As an adjective, huge: koca bir ev.

    A1

  23. 323
    sürmekverb

    to last, to take (time); to drive; to spread, to put on

    Film iki saat sürüyor.

    The movie is two hours long.

    aorist sürer · present sürüyor · past sürdü · future sürecek

    Also to drive (araba sürmek) and to spread (ekmeğe tereyağı sürmek). Ne kadar sürer? = How long does it take?

    B2First taught in B2 · Unit 5: Formal Turkish· Conjugation

  24. 324
    keznoun

    time (occasion)

    İstanbul'a ilk kez geliyorum.

    It's my first time in Istanbul.

    İki kez = twice; bu kez = this time. Defa and sefer mean the same.

    B1First taught in B1 · Unit 1: Past continuous and pluperfect

  25. 325
    ödemekverb

    to pay; to pay back

    Hesabı ben öderim.

    I'll pay the bill.

    aorist öder · present ödüyor · past ödedi · future ödeyecek

    The e becomes ü before -(I)yor: ödüyor. Kartla ödemek = to pay by card.

    A2First taught in A2 · Unit 11: While and then· Conjugation

  26. 326
    hemconjunction

    both … and (hem … hem); and also, besides

    Hem ucuz hem çok güzel.

    It's both cheap and really nice.

    Usually doubled: hem çay hem kahve (both tea and coffee). Hem de = and what's more.

    B2First taught in B2 · Unit 10: As long as, unless, in case

  27. 327
    falanadverb

    or so, about; and stuff, and so on; so-and-so (adj)

    Beş dakika falan bekledim.

    I waited five minutes or so.

    Casual. After a number, about; at the end of a list, and stuff: çay, kahve falan.

    B2First taught in B2 · Unit 9: Everyday colloquial Turkish

  28. 328
    elbetteadverb

    of course, certainly

    Elbette yardım ederim.

    Of course I'll help.

    A little more formal than tabii.

    A2

  29. 329
    ayrılmakverb

    to leave; to split up, to separate

    Ali ile Ayşe ayrıldı.

    Ali and Ayşe broke up.

    aorist ayrılır · present ayrılıyor · past ayrıldı · future ayrılacak

    The place or person you leave takes the ablative: evden ayrılmak, ondan ayrıldı (she left him).

    B1First taught in B1 · Unit 11: Causative and reciprocal· Conjugation

  30. 330
    yalannoun

    lie; false (adj)

    Bana yalan söyleme!

    Don't lie to me!

    Yalan söylemek = to lie; yalancı = liar.

    B1First taught in B1 · Unit 3: Hearsay and inference

  31. 331
    dışnoun

    outside, exterior; foreign (adj)

    Hafta sonu şehir dışına çıkıyoruz.

    We're going out of town this weekend.

    his, her, its dışı

    Mostly with endings: dışında (outside; except). Yurt dışı = abroad; dış ülkeler = foreign countries.

    A2First taught in A2 · Unit 9: Where and when: postpositions

  32. 332
    özeladjective

    special; private; personal

    Bu benim için çok özel bir gün.

    This is a very special day for me.

    Also private: özel okul (private school), özel hayat (private life).

  33. 333
    isimnoun

    name; noun (in grammar)

    Ne güzel bir isim!

    What a lovely name!

    accusative ismi

    The second i drops before a vowel: ismi, ismim. Ad means the same.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 9: My family

  34. 334
    hangideterminer

    which

    Hangi otobüs Taksim'e gidiyor?

    Which bus goes to Taksim?

    Hangisi? = Which one?

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 4: Questions and negation

    yalnızadjective

    alone; lonely; only, just (adv)

    Yalnız mı yaşıyorsun?

    Also only, just: Yalnız bir sorun var (There's just one problem). Yalnızlık = loneliness.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 5: Where things are

  36. 336
    kannoun

    blood

    Parmağımdan kan geliyor.

    My finger is bleeding.

    Kan grubu = blood type; kanamak = to bleed.

  37. 337
    karınoun

    wife (colloquial)

    Bu benim karım, Fatma.

    This is my wife, Fatma.

    Colloquial, and can sound rude; eşim is the neutral, polite word. Karı koca = husband and wife.

    A2

  38. 338
    aşknoun

    love (romantic); passion

    İlk görüşte aşka inanır mısın?

    Do you believe in love at first sight?

    Romantic love; sevgi is love in general. Aşkım = my love. Âşık olmak = to fall in love.

    C1First taught in C1 · Unit 4: Ottoman, Arabic and Persian structures

  39. 339
    uzakadjective

    far, distant

    Havalimanı buradan uzak mı?

    Uzakta = far away. The opposite is yakın.

  40. 340
    vakitnoun

    time

    Vakit yok, acele et!

    There's no time, hurry up!

    accusative vakti

    The i drops before a vowel: vakti, vaktim. Means the same as zaman.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 9: My family

  41. 341
    şehirnoun

    city; town

    Şehir merkezine nasıl gidebilirim?

    How can I get to the city centre?

    accusative şehri

    The i drops before a vowel (şehri, şehre) but not before a consonant (şehirde). Kent is a more formal word.

  42. 342
    parçanoun

    piece, part; track, song

    Bana bir parça ekmek ver.

    Give me a piece of bread.

    Also a piece of music: Bu parça çok güzel (This song is great).

    sabahnoun

    morning; in the morning

    I get up early in the morning.

    kalkmakverb

    to get up, to stand up; to leave, to depart (of vehicles)

    Tren saat kaçta kalkıyor?

    What time does the train leave?

    aorist kalkar · present kalkıyor · past kalktı · future kalkacak

    Erken kalkmak = to get up early; ayağa kalkmak = to stand up.

    ayrıcaadverb

    also, in addition; besides

    Adds one more point, like besides or what's more.

  46. 346
    filmnoun

    film, movie

    Bu akşam sinemada hangi film var?

    What movie is playing tonight?

    Film çekmek = to shoot a film; a TV series is a dizi.

    beripostposition

    since; for (up to now)

    Sabahtan beri seni arıyorum.

    I've been looking for you since this morning.

    After the ablative: sabahtan beri (since this morning), iki yıldan beri (for two years). The verb stays in the present: bekliyorum (I've been waiting).

  48. 348
    merak etmekverb

    to wonder, to be curious; to worry

    Merak etme, ben iyiyim.

    Don't worry, I'm fine.

    aorist merak eder · present merak ediyor · past merak etti · future merak edecek

    Merak etme! = Don't worry! What you wonder about takes the accusative: sonucu merak ediyorum. Meraklı = curious.

    ateşnoun

    fire; fever

    Çocuğun ateşi var.

    havanoun

    weather; air

    dünadverb

    yesterday

    Where were you yesterday evening?

    Dün gece = last night; dünkü = yesterday's.

    Size nasıl yardımcı olabilirim?

    How can I help you?

    Yardımcı olmak = to help (polite), with the dative. As a noun, assistant.

    A2

  82. 382
    kaçırmakverb

    to miss (a bus, a chance); to kidnap; to let slip

    Otobüsü kaçırdım!

    I missed the bus!

    aorist kaçırır · present kaçırıyor · past kaçırdı · future kaçıracak

    The causative of kaçmak. Also to kidnap, frequent in films.

    A2First taught in A2 · Unit 1: The past tense

  83. 383
    ayaknoun

    foot; leg (of furniture)

    Ayağım çok ağrıyor.

    My foot really hurts.

    accusative ayağı

    k becomes ğ before a vowel: ayağı. Ayağa kalkmak = to stand up.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 9: My family

  84. 384
    yaramakverb

    to be useful, to be good for; to do good

    Bu ne işe yarar?

    What's this for?

    aorist yarar · present yarıyor · past yaradı · future yarayacak

    Mostly in işe yaramak (to be of use): Hiçbir işe yaramıyor (It's no use at all). Yaramaz = naughty.

    B1

  85. 385
    nefret etmekverb

    to hate

    Yalandan nefret ederim.

    I hate lies.

    aorist nefret eder · present nefret ediyor · past nefret etti · future nefret edecek

    What you hate takes the ablative: senden nefret ediyorum.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 7: To and from

  86. 386
    bilginoun

    information; knowledge

    Daha fazla bilgi için bizi arayın.

    For more information, call us.

    Bilgisayar (computer) is built on it.

    B1First taught in B1 · Unit 3: Hearsay and inference

  87. 387
    suçnoun

    crime, offence; fault, blame

    Bu benim suçum değil!

    It's not my fault!

    accusative suçu

    Both a crime and the blame: Suç kimde? (Whose fault is it?). Suçlu = guilty.

    A2

  88. 388
    yüznumber

    hundred

    Bu ayakkabılar yüz lira.

    These shoes are a hundred lira.

    No bir before it: yüz (a hundred), iki yüz (two hundred). The noun yüz means face.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 11: Numbers and time

  89. 389
    geminoun

    ship

    Gemi limandan saat onda kalkıyor.

    The ship leaves the port at ten.

    A ferry is a vapur; a small boat a tekne.

    B2First taught in B2 · Unit 1: Unreal conditionals and wishes

  90. 390
    kolayadjective

    easy

    Bu soru çok kolay.

    This question is very easy.

    Kolay gelsin! is said to someone at work, roughly hope it goes well. The opposite is zor.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 4: Questions and negation

  91. 391
    sankiconjunction

    as if, as though

    Sanki bir rüyadayım.

    It's like I'm in a dream.

    Written as one word, like belki and çünkü.

    B2First taught in B2 · Unit 2: As if

  92. 392
    ölümnoun

    death

    Bu bir ölüm kalım meselesi.

    This is a matter of life and death.

    From ölmek (to die).

    B1

  93. 393
    bitirmekverb

    to finish, to complete

    Ödevini bitirdin mi?

    Have you finished your homework?

    aorist bitirir · present bitiriyor · past bitirdi · future bitirecek

    You finish something; for something that ends by itself, use bitmek. Okulu bitirmek = to graduate.

    A2First taught in A2 · Unit 1: The past tense

  94. 394
    veyaconjunction

    or

    Yarın veya cuma günü gelirim.

    I'll come tomorrow or on Friday.

    To offer a choice in a question, Turkish prefers mı … mı: Çay mı, kahve mi? Ya da means the same as veya.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 12: Requests and company

  95. 395
    sağlamakverb

    to provide, to supply; to ensure

    Okul öğrencilere ücretsiz kitap sağlar.

    The school provides free books to students.

    aorist sağlar · present sağlıyor · past sağladı · future sağlayacak

    Formal. The a becomes ı before -(I)yor: sağlıyor.

    B2First taught in B2 · Unit 7: Stacked voices

  96. 396
    satmakverb

    to sell

    Eski arabamızı sattık.

    We sold our old car.

    aorist satar · present satıyor · past sattı · future satacak

    Satın almak = to buy; satılık = for sale.

    A2First taught in A2 · Unit 12: Word building

  97. 397
    çekilmekverb

    to move aside, to step back; to withdraw, to resign; to be pulled, to be taken

    Önümden çekil, lütfen.

    Please get out of my way.

    aorist çekilir · present çekiliyor · past çekildi · future çekilecek

    Çekil! = Get out of the way! Also the passive of çekmek: Bu fotoğraf İzmir'de çekildi (This photo was taken in Izmir).

    B1

  98. 398
    yerinepostposition

    instead of; in place of

    Kahve yerine çay içer misin?

    Would you have tea instead of coffee?

    From yer (place). With pronouns, a possessive: benim yerime (instead of me).

    B1First taught in B1 · Unit 2: Used to, was going to, should have

  99. 399
    beynoun

    Mr (after a first name); gentleman

    Ahmet Bey burada mı?

    Is Mr Ahmet here?

    Polite title after a man's first name: Mehmet Bey. Before a surname, in writing, Bay. Beyefendi = sir.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 3: Saying who you are

  100. 400
    kitapnoun

    book

    Bu kitabı okudun mu?

    Have you read this book?

    accusative kitabı

    p becomes b before a vowel: kitabı, kitabım. Kitapçı = bookshop.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 2: Vowel harmony and plurals

About this list

The words are ranked by how often they come up in film and TV dialogue, so the list leans towards spoken Turkish. Words are listed in their dictionary form (verbs in the infinitive, gelmek), names and fragments are left out, and ranks are estimates rather than exact counts.

The order of the list is adapted from the 2018 Turkish list of FrequencyWords by Hermit Dave, made from the OpenSubtitles2018 corpus via OPUS, and is licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0. The meanings, example sentences and notes are original to Daily Turkish.
